PC games live one per folder. Pick the root folder that holds them — Elyndra scans it folder by folder and finds each game\'s executable on its own. It also picks up the shortcuts a Windows runtime exports for frontends (.desktop, .steam…), which is what actually starts the game. Or a folder of ID files: one file per game (.iso, .txt, .steam) named after the game and holding only its BannerHub ID.

No games found. Each game needs its own folder with its .exe inside; pick the folder that contains them all, not one game\'s folder. A folder of shortcuts exported from your Windows runtime works too. Or a folder of ID files: one file per game (.iso, .txt, .steam) whose content is just the BannerHub ID.
%1$s can\'t be handed a game from outside, so Elyndra just opens it — pick the game there, in its own container.
%1$s is handed the shortcut it exports for frontends (.desktop, .steam…), not the .exe. Pick the folder where %1$s writes them.

BannerHub, GameHub and GameNative only start games that are already in their own library, each one with its ID. Type the ID of this game — the number on its page inside the runtime (a Steam game uses its appid: 268910, 2551…). Leave it blank to remove it.
Which installed build the games are sent to
%1$s will be taken out of the library. The file stays on your storage, and a rescan will not bring it back — you can restore it from the folder menu.
Ask Masha, or tell her what to do…
Masha here. I know your library, how you play and what your phone can handle. Ask me anything — or just tell me how much time you’ve got.
No DeepSeek key yet, so I’m answering locally.

DeepSeek rejected the API key. Check it in Settings → Masha.
The DeepSeek account has no balance left. Answering offline meanwhile.
DeepSeek says slow down. Give me a moment.

That got tangled on my side. Try asking another way.
